Date: 2026-06-02
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Verdure Head of AI Ops), Dr. Samir Rao (CTO), Asha Patel (Procurement)
Recording: yes
Notes: renewal + capacity bump; discuss EU region private pilot and contract amendment
summary: Check-in focused on Verdure Health's upcoming renewal and planned capacity expansion to support new clinical triage product. Discussion covered options for EU private/onprem pilot vs Redwood Dedicated burst, latency targets, cost tradeoffs, and timeline for contracting. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share updated pricing and EU SKU options; SE to run a 48-hour perf benchmark on Verdure staging set; Verdure to confirm procurement stakeholders and internal timeline.
topics: Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem) for EU data residency
Throughput & latency targets for clinical triage workload
Autoscaling and burst policy for peak hours
Security controls: SOC2 audit, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for carving time. We usually do a quick agenda — contract status, capacity ask, and next steps. Lena, Samir, you good?
[00:15] Lena (Verdure): Yep, thanks Maya. Quick yes. Sorry for the slight delay, some folks jammed on another call.
[00:28] Samir (CTO): Morning/afternoon all. We're mostly focused on two things: we want to avoid a gap at renewal and we need more regional capacity in EU for the triage model.
[00:42] Maya: Got it. We showed initial numbers in the renewal deck; today we want to align on how much committed capacity, and whether you want a Private pilot or Redwood Dedicated in eu-west.
[00:55] Asha (Procurement): Before we start, can you confirm contract term options? We need 12 vs 24 month pricing.
[01:05] Maya: Sure — we can do a 12 month renewal with an optional 12 month extension clause, or a 24 month at a discount. I'll send the amendment templates after.
[01:20] Ethan (SE): Quick technical note — for your clinical triage workload we've seen best throughput with continuous batching + prefix cache. We can quantify during the benchmark.
[01:35] Lena: Important: EU data residency is non-negotiable for this product — logs and models must stay in region; also our compliance team is pushing for customer-managed KMS.
[01:50] Ethan: Understood. We have Private (VPC) and on-prem options. For KMS you can bring your own key via our KMS integration; audit logs are available per-token and per-route. There's one caveat — onprem path takes a few weeks to provision.
[02:05] Samir: How much lead time? We have a security review scheduled by the 10th of June.
[02:14] Ethan: For a VPC private deployment in eu-west, typical lead is 2–3 weeks to initial activation and a longer on-prem package if you need air-gapped. But for Dedicated reserved capacity we can stand up capacity in region in 5–7 business days if inventory available.
[02:30] Lena: Hm okay. The triage model has a peak pattern — 4x spikes during morning clinics. We need a fallback if dedicated capacity is saturated.
[02:42] Maya: We recommend a routing policy: Primary -> Dedicated EU pool; fallback -> hosted geo-compatible model (slightly smaller). That keeps latency SLOs during bursts.
[02:55] Asha: Pricing for fallback? If they spill to hosted, how is that billed?
[03:07] Maya: We'll charge per-token on the hosted usage, but we can include capped spillover rates in the contract for predictability. We'll put the proposal in the pricing sheet.
[03:20] Samir: On latency — we need 95th percentile under 220ms for single-turn inference at 512 tokens. Possible?
[03:34] Ethan: 220ms P95 for 512 tokens is aggressive but achievable on dedicated with optimized kernels and reduced batching window. If you go private/onprem with proper GPU class we can meet it more consistently. But cost is higher.
[03:48] Lena: Can you quantify cost delta between Dedicated and Private? Ballpark for committed 100k tokens/day?
[03:58] Maya: Ballpark: Dedicated reserved capacity typically yields a 30–40% unit cost improvement vs on-demand hosted; Private has higher fixed platform/license + ops support — rough delta 15–25% higher than Dedicated depending on HW. I'll add concrete numbers to the sheet.
[04:15] Samir: Another key item — KV cache warming for commonly seen prefixes from our EMR ingestion. We can't afford cold-start latencies.
[04:28] Ethan: We'll include prefix caching policy and suggest a warm-up job during off-peak. Also recommend prefill using your historical logs so KV cache warms quickly. There might be minor privacy concerns so we'll advise on pseudonymization.
[04:45] Lena: For the EU private pilot, do you support our compliance scanners and quarterly SOC2 evidence?
[04:55] Maya: Yes, SOC2 reports are available; for private deployments we can provide more detailed artifacts. We'll share the SOC2 and ISO docs link after the call.
[05:07] Asha: Procurement question — can we get a payment schedule tied to milestones? We prefer quarterly invoicing aligned to activation and the pilot success metric.
[05:18] Maya: Absolutely, milestone billing is common; we'll propose an activation milestone + 30/60/90 day payments in the draft amendment.
[05:30] Lena: Back to capacity — our expected steady state is 60k tokens/day but with spikes to 240k on clinic mornings. We want autoscale to handle spikes but maintain cost predictability. Thoughts?
[05:45] Ethan: Autoscale + burst pool works well. One configuration is reserve baseline for steady 60k and configure burst credits/capacity for peak; plus a hard cap to avoid runaway spend. We'll include simulated spend charts in the pricing workbook.
[06:02] Samir: For the benchmark, can you replicate our weighted distribution? We have a mix: 70% short prompts (~64 tokens), 30% medium (256–512 tokens).
[06:15] Ethan: Yes, have your staging set and we'll replay it. If you share a 10k sample we can do a 48 hour run and return P50/P95, throughput, and token-cost deltas.
[06:28] Lena: We'll upload to the shared S3 staging bucket and invite Redwood's service account.
[06:34] Maya: Great. We'll confirm IAM perms after the call.
[06:42] Asha: Any competitors we should be aware of? Our security folks asked if BigCloudAI or ModelServeX offers cheaper private pods.
[06:52] Maya: They do; ModelServeX does private with a lower headline price but less observability and fewer rollout tools. We trade a bit on raw price for better tooling and latency guarantees. We'll include a competitor comparison in a short doc.
[07:06] Samir: SLA questions — what's the emergency escalation path if we see model regressions during rollout?
[07:16] Ethan: We have rollback + canary + automatic fallback policies. Also a dedicated oncall for Dedicated customers; for Private there's an ops package. We'll document RTO/RTS in the SLA exhibit.
[07:30] Lena: On data retention — we only want logs retained for 30 days in EU. Is that configurable?
[07:38] Ethan: Yes, retention is configurable per-customer; for private we can set retention at 30 days and scrub tokens based on your policy.
[07:46] Maya: Recap so far: Verdure wants 12–24 month contract with committed baseline ~60k tokens/day and burst to 240k; EU residency and KMS BYOK; 220ms P95 target; bench run and pricing + amendment to be shared.
[07:58] Samir: Sounds right. A few smaller clarifications — does Redwood provide model quantization recommendations? We've seen cost drop when we move to int8 variants.
[08:10] Ethan: Yes, Optimize can recommend quantization and we've tested int8 paths with small quality checks. We'll include expected quality delta and fallback to fp16 if necessary.
[08:24] Lena: Timeline — we need procurement signed before June 20. Is that doable?
[08:31] Maya: Tight but doable if we turn the amendment quickly. That's why we'll put a short 'execute by' incentive in the draft.
[08:40] Asha: On the contract clause about spillover caps — we need a hard upper limit on hosted spill tokens per month.
[08:50] Maya: We'll propose a capped spill allowance; if you exceed it, we escalate cost to on-demand rates. We'll make the cap conservative to avoid surprises.
[09:02] Samir: For the Private pilot, are there any network prerequisites on our side?
[09:09] Ethan: For VPC private we need route tables, an allowed egress to our control plane endpoints and an agreed set of ports for the data plane; we'll provide a network checklist. For on-prem, we'll need firewall rules and a BGP peering plan if you're doing east-west.
[09:24] Lena: Good. Please send the network checklist and I'll loop in infra.
[09:28] Maya: Will do.
[09:30] Ethan: One small note — if you go Dedicated but later decide Private, we have migration playbooks but expect a migration window and possible revalidation of keys.
[09:42] Samir: That's fine. As long as it's documented.
[09:46] Maya: Okay quick timeline recap and owners: pricing + amendment (Maya) by 6/5; perf benchmark (Ethan) by 6/6; Verdure confirms procurement/stakeholders (Lena/Asha) by 6/4. Then we aim exec signing call week of 6/8.
[10:02] Asha: Confirmed. We'll try to accelerate internal signoff.
[10:07] Lena: Also, can we get a sample audit log extract to pass to our compliance folks?
[10:14] Ethan: Yes, we'll redact customer data and provide a sample log export.
[10:19] Maya: Anything else?
[10:22] Samir: Not from me. Thanks — and thanks for the flexible billing options.
[10:27] Maya: Great. I'm going to follow up with the link to the pricing workbook and SOC2/ISO docs.
[10:33] Lena: Thanks everyone.
[10:36] Maya: Thanks, bye.
[10:40] End of recording

Notes: transcript contains small ASR errors (product names occasionally garbled, punctuation inconsistent). Links mentioned: pricing workbook (internal) and SOC2 docs https://redwood.example/soc2 and network checklist https://redwood.example/network-checklist.
